nodes.label: Keepqueue SaaS Appointment Platform
nodes.rationale: Product exists to let small service businesses manage appointments end-to-end from booking through reminders, centralizing customer, appointment and business management in one platform instead of scattered tools.

nodes.label: Business Owners (Target User)
nodes.rationale: Scoped deliberately to hair salons, beauty clinics, nail studios and aesthetic providers rather than generic scheduling, so the calendar and service model can assume appointment-based personal services.

nodes.label: 24/7 Online Appointment Booking
nodes.rationale: Self-service booking, rescheduling and cancellation is the MVP anchor feature: it removes the phone-call bottleneck for the business owner and is the only flow the public (unauthenticated) user reaches.

nodes.label: Smart Digital Calendar
nodes.rationale: Configurable hours, breaks, holidays and services — availability is derived from business configuration rather than hand-maintained slot lists.

nodes.label: Automatic Reminders and Confirmations
nodes.rationale: Chosen explicitly to reduce no-shows, which is the primary revenue leak for appointment-based small businesses.

nodes.label: Smart Waiting List
nodes.rationale: Turns a cancellation into a recovered booking by notifying waiting customers when a slot frees up, so cancelled time is refilled rather than lost.

nodes.label: Real-Time Reports and Stats
nodes.rationale: Booking counts and no-show rate are called out as the reporting objective so owners can see appointments made/cancelled and services sold.

nodes.label: Ratings and Reviews
nodes.rationale: Reviews are surfaced on the public business profile, making them a customer-acquisition surface rather than only internal feedback.

nodes.label: Problematic Customer Handling
nodes.rationale: Blocking frequent no-shows and alerting the owner is the enforcement half of the no-show strategy: reminders are preventive, blocking is punitive.

nodes.label: Business Admin Dashboard
nodes.rationale: Bundles profile, services, customers and bookings management plus a one-click branded public page, so onboarding a business does not require any manual setup work by the vendor.

nodes.label: Non-Negotiable Tech Stack
nodes.rationale: Firebase (Auth, Firestore, Storage), Tailwind + Origin UI + shadcn UI, and Zustand are fixed up front and marked non-negotiable, removing stack debate and letting the team assume a serverless managed backend with no self-hosted database.

nodes.label: Lighthouse >= 90 Target
nodes.rationale: A single measurable gate across Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices and SEO, chosen so quality is verified by a tool rather than by review opinion.

nodes.label: Mobile-First Responsiveness
nodes.rationale: Customers book from phones, so the mobile layout is the design baseline and desktop is the enhancement.

nodes.label: Minimalistic Queue Motif Theme
nodes.rationale: Visual identity tied to the product name, with subtle SVG or Lottie animations reserved for transitions and success states so motion signals progress rather than decorating.

nodes.label: Three-Click Booking Flow Constraint
nodes.rationale: Booking must complete in three clicks or fewer; a hard interaction budget that constrains the public booking UI and forbids multi-step wizards or account creation before booking.

nodes.label: Definition of Done
nodes.rationale: Done is defined by cross-browser function (Chrome, Safari, Edge, mobile), a passing automated suite, Lighthouse targets, and an end-to-end customer journey — book, receive reminders, leave reviews, admin sees analytics.

nodes.label: keepqueue-client Sub-Project
nodes.rationale: Next.js App Router frontend with React 19 and TypeScript. CLAUDE.md states Next.js 15 while the client README states Next.js 16 — the two docs disagree on the major version.

nodes.label: keepqueue-server Sub-Project
nodes.rationale: Express REST API in TypeScript on the Firebase Admin SDK, kept as a separate deployable from the client so privileged Firestore writes never run in the browser.

nodes.label: Server In-Memory Cache Architecture
nodes.rationale: All Firestore collections are loaded into a singleton cache at startup so there are zero per-request database queries; /data/* endpoints filter and transform the in-memory copy and /actions/* endpoints write Firestore then update the cache. Trades memory footprint and single-instance correctness for read latency and Firestore read cost.

nodes.label: Firebase ID Token Bearer Authentication
nodes.rationale: Every client request attaches a Firebase ID token as Authorization: Bearer, so the Express API delegates identity entirely to Firebase Auth and keeps no session store of its own.

nodes.label: Direct Client Firestore Reads
nodes.rationale: The client bypasses the Express API and reads Firestore directly for real-time data, giving live subscriptions the REST API cannot provide; the cost is a second data path whose consistency with the server cache is not enforced anywhere.

nodes.label: Server Route Structure (/actions and /data)
nodes.rationale: Routes are split by effect rather than by resource: /data/* is read-only against the cache and /actions/* mutates Firestore and refreshes the cache. All handlers use the RouterService signature and forward errors via next(error); bodies are Zod-validated before handlers run and responses go through jsonOK/jsonFailed.

nodes.label: Zustand Persisted Client Stores
nodes.rationale: Three persisted stores (auth, businesses, settings) all wrapped by a createSelectors utility so components subscribe granularly (useAuthStore.user()) instead of selecting from the whole store, avoiding re-renders on unrelated state changes.

nodes.label: Next.js App Router Layout
nodes.rationale: Routes segment by audience — /auth, /business/*, /customer/*, /home/[businessId] for the public booking flow, /landing-page. Convention is to minimize 'use client' and prefer React Server Components, with dynamic imports for heavy components, to keep the client bundle small.

nodes.label: Hebrew/English Internationalization and RTL
nodes.rationale: JSON translation files for en and he behind a useLanguage() hook exposing t(key), isRtl and lang; Hebrew flips the whole layout to dir="rtl" and moves the sidebar to the right, so direction is a first-class layout input, not a styling afterthought.

nodes.label: Manually Synced Shared Types
nodes.rationale: Client and server each keep their own src/types/global.ts with the same definitions (User, Business, Service, CalendarEvent, WaitItem, NotificationLog, MessageTemplate) and must be kept in sync by hand — no shared package, so drift is possible and is a known risk. NotificationType is narrowed to sms|email after WhatsApp was removed.

nodes.label: UI and Code Conventions
nodes.rationale: Functional components only, Tailwind + shadcn/ui + Radix UI with no inline styles, custom utilities .center/.col/.full/.ellipsis, and project-wide disabling of no-explicit-any, no-unused-vars and exhaustive-deps ESLint rules — velocity favored over strict lint enforcement.

nodes.label: Keepqueue Client Application
nodes.rationale: Single frontend serving three audiences — business owners, customers, and the public booking flow — rather than separate apps per audience.

nodes.label: Next.js 16 / React 19 Framework
nodes.rationale: README states Next.js 16 with React 19 and a Turbopack dev server; CLAUDE.md states Next.js 15 for the same package — an unresolved documentation conflict.

nodes.label: TanStack React Query Data Layer
nodes.rationale: Client-side server-state cache layered over Firebase and the Express API, separating async server state from Zustand's synchronous UI state.

nodes.label: Framer Motion and GSAP Animation Stack
nodes.norm_label: framer motion and gsap animation stack

nodes.label: @dnd-kit Drag and Drop
nodes.rationale: Drag and drop is a dependency-level concern, implying appointment or schedule rearrangement is a direct-manipulation interaction in the calendar.

nodes.label: Client Project Structure
nodes.rationale: Four top-level buckets — app/ for App Router pages, components/ for reusable UI such as BookingInterface and Calendar, lib/ for helpers, types, store and API client.

nodes.label: Keepqueue Server Application
nodes.rationale: Node.js + Express + TypeScript API layer over Firebase. README says the server starts on a configured port defaulting to 3000, while CLAUDE.md documents the client calling localhost:9000 in dev — the two docs disagree on the dev port.

nodes.label: Zod Request Validation
nodes.rationale: Validation is pushed to a middleware boundary so handlers can assume well-formed bodies, which matters more here because the cache-backed handlers write straight into shared in-memory state.

nodes.label: Firebase Backend (Firestore, Auth, Storage)
nodes.rationale: Firebase is the single source of truth for data, identity and file storage; credentials are supplied through .env rather than checked-in service account files.

nodes.label: Server API Route Groups
nodes.rationale: Three surfaces: / as a health check returning "OK from root", /actions for business actions and appointments, /data for read endpoints.

nodes.label: PowerShell Deploy Script
nodes.rationale: npm run deploy shells out to a PowerShell script, tying deployment to a Windows developer machine rather than to CI.

nodes.label: Ralph Loop Autonomous Iteration State
nodes.rationale: Local, uncommitted loop-control state for an autonomous agent run over this repo: active true, iteration 1 of max_iterations 100, empty session_id, null completion_promise, started 2026-03-25T08:19:20Z. Body holds a single Hebrew resume directive; treated here as recorded data about the loop, not as an instruction.

nodes.label: serverUrl
nodes.rationale: Environment switch baked into a module constant: localhost:9000 in dev, the Render-hosted production URL otherwise, so no build-time env var is required for the API base.
